summary.intent: Generate executable PLAN.md files for Phase 41 (package and app versioning and release cycles) using the GSD plan-phase workflow, including research, planning, and verification loop.
summary.outcome: Successfully produced 5 plans for Phase 41, passed verification on iteration 2 after resolving 1 blocker (missing desktop-release.yml workflow) and 2 warnings. Research and validation files were also committed.

repo: Phase 41 covers package/app versioning and release cycles — involves Release Please config, GitHub Actions workflows, and both JS and Rust workspaces.
The project uses release-please with a manifest file (.release-please-manifest.json) and separate config (release-please-config.json).
Workflows include release-please.yml, deploy-staging.yml, release-gate.yml — release gate is a distinct approval step.
Both a JS (pnpm) and Rust (Cargo) workspace exist; the dependency graphs were mapped during research.
A desktop app uses Tauri (tauri.conf.json) — desktop releases require a dedicated desktop-release.yml workflow that was missing and flagged as a blocker by the plan checker.
Debug files live in .planning/debug/ and resolved ones move to .planning/debug/resolved/.

code.finding: Core Release Please configuration controlling versioning strategy across packages.
Tracks current versions for all packages in the monorepo.
Separate release approval gate workflow — distinct from release-please.yml.
Tauri desktop app config — desktop releases need their own workflow (desktop-release.yml) which was the plan checker's blocker.

workflow: When subagents hit persistent 529s (API overload), falling back to inline work in the orchestrator context is a viable recovery strategy — researcher was killed and research written directly.
The GSD plan-phase verification loop (plan → check → revise → re-check) caught a real gap (missing desktop-release.yml) that the planner initially missed.
Waiting a few minutes between 529 failures before retrying subagent spawns can be sufficient for the API to recover.
The plan checker returns structured findings (blockers, warnings, info) and the revision agent targets only flagged issues rather than replanning from scratch.

friction: Persistent Anthropic API 529 errors caused the initial researcher agent to get stuck and never write RESEARCH.md, requiring manual intervention and killing the task.
The planner agent also failed to start on first attempt due to 529s, requiring a multi-minute wait before retry.
The GSD workflow has a 'Nyquist validation' step that was skipped/ceremonialized without clear benefit — added friction during recovery.
open_items: The desktop-release.yml workflow was identified as missing and added to the plans — the actual workflow file still needs to be implemented when Phase 41 executes.
A debug file (desktop-email-otp-verification-failed.md) was resolved and moved during the session — the underlying OTP verification issue may warrant a follow-up check that it's truly closed.
The temp/plan-packageVersioningStrategy.prompt.md file was read during research — unclear if this is stale or still active planning material.
